prompt.system: You answer questions about tides and water levels in Canada using the tools. Never guess tide times or heights; call a tool. The current time is 2026-11-25 12:00 UTC. Find the station first with find_stations unless you already have its code. Tool results include local times for the station; give times to the user in that local time and say which station you used. If a tool returns an error, say plainly what went wrong instead of making up an answer. Keep answers short.
prompt.question: Should I launch a canoe at Tofino tomorrow morning?

tools.name: find_stations
tools.description:
Find tide gauge stations by place name, or the nearest ones to a point.

        Give `query` (for example "Halifax" or "Saint John"), or both `latitude`
        and `longitude`. With coordinates, results are sorted by distance. Each
        result has the station `code` to use in the other tools, its time zone,
        and which data series it has: wlo (observed water level), wlp (predicted
        water level), wlp-hilo (predicted high and low tides).

        Args:
            query: Part of a station name. Case does not matter.
            latitude: Degrees north, -90 to 90. Needs longitude.
            longitude: Degrees east, -180 to 180 (west is negative). Needs latitude.
            limit: How many stations to return, 1 to 20.
            max_distance_km: Drop stations farther than this from the point.
            include_inactive: Also list stations that are not operating.

tools.name: get_water_levels
tools.description:
Get observed (measured) water levels for a station over a time range.

        Returns a summary (highest, lowest, mean) and the points. Some stations
        do not report observed levels, and a station can go quiet for a while;
        the error says so. For the future, use get_tide_predictions instead.

        Args:
            station: Station code like "07735" or a name like "Vancouver".
            start: Start time. "2026-11-24" (whole local day), "2026-11-24T08:00"
                (station local time), "2026-11-24T16:00:00Z" (UTC) or "now".
            end: End time, same formats. A date alone means the end of that day.
                At most 7 days after start.
            resolution_minutes: 15 or 60. At most 200 points are returned.

tools.name: get_tide_predictions
tools.description:
Get predicted water levels (the tide table curve) for a station.

        Same inputs and output shape as get_water_levels. Predictions come from
        harmonic analysis and do not include weather. To find just the next high
        and low tides, next_high_low_tide is shorter.

        Args:
            station: Station code like "00490" or a name like "Halifax".
            start: Start time. "2026-11-26" (whole local day), "2026-11-26T08:00"
                (station local time), "2026-11-26T12:00:00Z" (UTC) or "now".
            end: End time, same formats. A date alone means the end of that day.
                At most 7 days after start.
            resolution_minutes: 15 or 60. At most 200 points are returned.

tools.name: next_high_low_tide
tools.description:
List the next predicted high and low tides at a station.

        Each event says whether it is a high or a low, the time (UTC and local)
        and the height. To answer "when is high tide tomorrow", pass
        after="<tomorrow's date>" and read the events that fall on that day;
        ask for enough events (count=6 or more) to cover the whole day.

        Args:
            station: Station code like "00490" or a name like "Halifax".
            after: Where to start looking: "now", a date, or a date and time.
            count: How many events to return, 1 to 12.

tools.name: compare_observed_vs_predicted
tools.description:
Compare measured water levels with the predicted tide.

        Returns the average difference, root-mean-square difference and the
        largest gap (observed minus predicted). Large gaps usually come from
        storm surge, wind or river flow. Needs a station with both observed
        and predicted series, and a time range in the past.

        Args:
            station: Station code or name.
            start: Start time (same formats as get_water_levels).
            end: End time. At most 7 days after start.

tools.name: get_marine_forecast
tools.description:
Get the Environment Canada marine weather forecast for the water at a station.

        Returns the text forecast for the marine area the station is in: wind
        (in knots), weather, visibility, air temperature, freezing spray, and any
        marine warnings such as gale or small craft warnings. The forecast
        covers roughly the next 24 to 36 hours and is only for the next day or
        so. There is no forecast for inland stations, and some areas have none
        in winter. Use get_hourly_weather for wind hour by hour.

        Args:
            station: Station code like "00490" or a name like "Halifax".

tools.name: get_hourly_weather
tools.description:
Get the hourly weather forecast near a station: wind, temperature, rain chance.

        Uses the nearest Environment Canada city forecast point. Wind is given in
        km/h and in knots. The forecast only covers about the next 24 hours; the
        error tells you the window if you ask outside it. Also returns sunrise
        and sunset. For a marine warning or the wind over open water, use
        get_marine_forecast as well.

        Args:
            station: Station code like "00490" or a name like "Halifax".
            start: Start time. "2026-11-26T06:00" (station local time),
                "2026-11-26T11:00:00Z" (UTC), a date alone (start of that
                local day) or "now".
            end: End time, same formats. A date alone means the end of that day.
                Defaults to 24 hours after start.

answer: No, I would not launch tomorrow morning. I used the Tofino station (08615). Environment Canada has a storm warning and a high water level warning in effect for West Coast Vancouver Island South. The marine forecast calls for southwest winds of 25 to 35 knots overnight, easing to about 25 knots near noon Thursday, with rain and a risk of thunderstorms. The hourly forecast for Tofino shows southwest wind of 22 knots (40 km/h), gusting to 60 km/h, from 06:00 to 12:00 local time, with showers and 100% chance of rain. That is far too much wind for a canoe. Tides (local times in the station data): low 08:06 at 1.69 m, high 14:04 at 4.00 m. A big tide swing on top of the high water warning would add to the risk. Wait for the warnings to end and the wind to drop well below 10 knots.
